svg.title: Base-Case Gross Billings to Owner Net Profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-profit-bridge; chart type: waterfall; title: Base-Case Gross Billings to Owner Net Profit; subtitle: $1,500,000 revenue less $1,305,000 costs leaves $195,000.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Annual USD. First bar is opening revenue; four negative bars are cost deductions; the sixth bar is the closing total, not an additional cash inflow. Cost allocations are illustrative; canonical scenario revenue and net profit remain fixed.; caption: Conservative: $500,000 × 8% = $40,000 with 5 FT + 6 C. Base: $1,500,000 × 13.0% = $195,000 with 5 FT + 6 C. Scaled: $2,500,000 × 18% = $450,000 with 6 FT + 7 C.; stages: label: Gross restoration billings; value: $1,500,000 opening revenue; 100%; numeric value: 1500000.0; detail: Recognized restoration contract revenue includes subcontracted work and materials. Do not substitute total claim value, property value, or cash advances.; label: Subcontractors and materials; value: −$795,000 direct costs; 53%; numeric value: -795000.0; detail: Charge actual contractor invoices and consumed materials to jobs. Six core contractor seats are capacity relationships, not six employee salaries.; label: Employee payroll and burden; value: −$270,000 employee costs; 18%; numeric value: -270000.0; detail: Illustrative loaded annual payroll for five full-time seats averages $54,000 per seat, including the working owner-manager seat where applicable.; label: Field operating costs; value: −$105,000 field operations; 7%; numeric value: -105000.0; detail: Allocate vehicle operation, equipment depreciation or rental, maintenance, consumables, and field safety costs without repeating direct material charges.; label: Administrative operating costs; value: −$135,000 administrative costs; 9%; numeric value: -135000.0; detail: Allocate facilities, insurance, dispatch software, estimating subscriptions, bookkeeping, marketing, and collection losses. Payroll, field, and administrative costs total $42,500 monthly, excluding variable direct costs.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $195,000 closing total; 13.0%; numeric value: 195000.0; detail: Subtract all four cost groups from gross revenue: $1,500,000 − $795,000 − $270,000 − $105,000 − $135,000 = $195,000. This is profit, not available cash before receivable collection.

text.title: Base-Case Gross Billings to Owner Net Profit
text.tspan: Base-Case Gross Billings to Owner Net Profit

rect.title: label: Gross restoration billings; value: $1,500,000 opening revenue; 100%; numeric value: 1500000.0; detail: Recognized restoration contract revenue includes subcontracted work and materials. Do not substitute total claim value, property value, or cash advances.

label: Subcontractors and materials; value: −$795,000 direct costs; 53%; numeric value: -795000.0; detail: Charge actual contractor invoices and consumed materials to jobs. Six core contractor seats are capacity relationships, not six employee salaries.

label: Employee payroll and burden; value: −$270,000 employee costs; 18%; numeric value: -270000.0; detail: Illustrative loaded annual payroll for five full-time seats averages $54,000 per seat, including the working owner-manager seat where applicable.

label: Field operating costs; value: −$105,000 field operations; 7%; numeric value: -105000.0; detail: Allocate vehicle operation, equipment depreciation or rental, maintenance, consumables, and field safety costs without repeating direct material charges.

label: Administrative operating costs; value: −$135,000 administrative costs; 9%; numeric value: -135000.0; detail: Allocate facilities, insurance, dispatch software, estimating subscriptions, bookkeeping, marketing, and collection losses. Payroll, field, and administrative costs total $42,500 monthly, excluding variable direct costs.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $195,000 closing total; 13.0%; numeric value: 195000.0; detail: Subtract all four cost groups from gross revenue: $1,500,000 − $795,000 − $270,000 − $105,000 − $135,000 = $195,000. This is profit, not available cash before receivable collection.

text.title: Assumptions: Annual USD. First bar is opening revenue; four negative bars are cost deductions; the sixth bar is the closing total, not an additional cash inflow. Cost allocations are illustrative; canonical scenario revenue and net profit remain fixed.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Annual USD. First bar is opening revenue; four negative bars are cost deductions; the sixth bar is the closing total,
